newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Three Timorese enter French embassy in Jakarta.
newsitem.headline: Three Timorese enter French embassy in Jakarta.

text.p: Three East Timorese men broke into the French embassy in Jakarta early on Tuesday, apparently to seek asylum, witnesses and Timorese sources said.

They said the three scaled the three metre (nine feet) spiked iron fence surrounding the French embassy compound and could be seen near the entrance waving a banner saying "Free East Timor" while gesturing and shouting "Viva East Timor".

Soon after they entered the compound at about 6 a.m. (2300 GMT Monday) a French official arrived and spoke to them. The three men handed over their identity cards, folded their banner and put it in a backpack that one of the men was carrying.
The embassy official told Reuters the men were East Timorese but he would not comment when asked if the three had sought asylum.
East Timorese sources said the three were seeking asylum in Portugal after being involved in a protest in the East Timor capital Dili on November 25.

A letter listing 10 demands on behalf of those seeking asylum, faxed to Reuters, appears to suggest the men had planned to enter the nearby Spanish embassy as the three-page document dated December 3 is addressed to the Spanish ambassador.
The letter calls for greater involvement of the United Nations in the East Timor question and a referendum over the future of the territory.
It was the latest in a series of break-ins at foreign missions in Jakarta by Timorese seeking to flee their troubled homeland.
At least 93 East Timorese have been granted asylum in Portugal since September last year after breaking into embassies in the Indonesian capital.

Indonesia invaded East Timor, a former Portuguese colony, in 1975 and annexed it a year later in an act not recognised by the United Nations. Many East Timorese oppose Jakarta's rule and accuse Indonesian troops in the territory of human rights abuses.
The French embassy in Jakarta, which recently extended its spiked iron fence, has been a particular target of break-ins. The latest is the ninth since November 1995.
Three East Timorese who were seen in the mission compound after a break-in on October 16 later said they were thrown out of the premises by an embassy official.
French embassy officials said no East Timorese had entered the mission.
